page.layout: One printed page of verse, centred in the main column, with a page number above the first line; at the right edge a narrow strip of margin notes belonging to the facing page (partly visible, cut off by the binding) which are not transcribed as they are not legible enough to read reliably. Below the last verse line, a word "Sic" at the right.

main_text.p: Ipse cubat medicus, cui sola Empirica cordi,
Et Methodus, sanum non habet ille caput;
Sed tua quod Themison ventosa cucurbita quærat.
Juppiter! hoc pereat cum Themisone genus.
Dogmaticusque velit se quivis doctor haberi,
Et medicus ferri clara per ora virûm,
Cui Logos in pretio. Phryx verò & barbarus esto.
Natura ingreditur cuius nunc templa minister
Strenuus; heicque acrem se probat esse virum.
Ille novos medicos (natta, vappaq, silete) Instituat; vacuo naviget amne Charon.
Nec pater ossa legat, nec tot modo funera mater:
Augeat aut censum trux Libitina suum.

page.notes: Marginal notes on the facing page strip at the right are cut off and illegible; not transcribed. The verse is set with indented lines; the stanza-like lines are rendered as printed. Some words are uncertain, notably "Dogmaticusque", "vappaq", and "Phryx" (the Greek-looking letters in the parenthesis are doubtful).
